title: Investigate billing ghost entries from project path aliasing during workspace merge
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Several customers reported unexplained 'ghost' usage billed to projects that had been merged or aliased. Initial triage shows duplicated metering writes for the same token under both the original and merged project IDs. Hypothesis: an ingress path aliasing flow combined with stale alias caches and asynchronous project-claim propagation allowed the metering pipeline to attribute the same request to two different project identifiers. Impact: incorrect invoices, inflated quotas, and potential rate-limit misapplication for affected tenants. This ticket captures investigation, remediation, and long-term fixes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create workspace A with project P-alpha and generate API token T-alpha.
2) Create workspace B with project P-beta and generate API token T-beta.
3) Merge P-alpha into P-beta using workspace-merge tool that creates a path alias mapping /p/alpha -> canonical /p/beta.
4) Send a burst of requests through the API gateway using the old token T-alpha immediately after merge while token-claim propagation is in flight.
5) Observe metering entries written to both project_id=P-alpha and project_id=P-beta in the metering write-ahead logs (WAL) for the same request IDs.
6) Confirm duplicate token attribution shows up in billing pipeline downstream and in per-project quota counters.
observations: - Gateway returns 200 and correct functional responses; user-visible behavior unaffected.
- Metering WAL contained duplicate writes for ~12k requests across 3 customers over a 6-hour window on 2026-02-24.
- Alias lookup cache TTLs in ingress (30s) were shorter than claim propagation window (several minutes) causing a window where both old and canonical mappings could be resolved concurrently.
- Metering service lacked idempotency keys for attribution writes when requests were re-routed or re-played by the gateway.
- Race between token-claim-service update and alias propagation in the gateway produced inconsistent mapping on read vs write paths.
mitigation: Short-term: set alias cache to strict-consistency mode for merges (disable multi-path resolution) and pause merges while token claims are propagated. Added emergency job to dedupe recent WAL entries and stop-gap correction to billing pipeline to reject duplicate attribution if request_id seen within 2 minutes.
resolution_plan: 1) Immediate (hotfix): Deploy gateway config change to prefer canonical project_id from central project-directory service and turn on single-path resolution (rolled to prod 2026-02-26). See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4823.

2) Mid-term: Add per-request metering idempotency key (combination of request_id + token_id) at ingress so metering writes are deduplicated in WAL. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Idempotent+Metering+Writes.
3) Long-term: Rework merge workflow to acquire distributed merge lock, block traffic for a short drain window, and atomically update alias mappings + token claims (release: billing-2026.06).
4) Backfill: Run a reconciler job to collapse duplicate windows and emit corrected billing adjustments for affected customers; coordinate with finance for refunds/credits.
comments: 2026-02-25: Aisha Kumar - Initial triage: customer support escalated 3 customers. Reproduced locally by simulating merge traffic; confirmed duplicate writes in local WAL. Opening ticket and assigning to Diego.

2026-02-26: Diego Martinez - Hotfix applied: gateway rolled with single-path alias resolution (config id: alias-mode=canonical-only). Early signals show a drop to zero duplicates on prod shard-3. Still seeing historic duplicates in WAL; starting dedupe job.
2026-02-27: SRE (Liu Chen) - Deployed WAL dedupe job to staging. Job idempotently marks duplicates and emits correction records. Load test shows deduper handles 50k events/min with <30s latency.
2026-03-01: PM (Riley Thompson) - Customer comms drafted. Proposed credits template and timeline for reconciliations. Finance looped in (ticket FIN-2026-45).

2026-03-04: Diego Martinez - Design decision: we'll add idempotency keys at ingress rather than patching every downstream writer. Trade-off: small increase in request metadata size vs significant simplification of reconciliation logic. Design doc linked in attachments.

2026-03-08: QA (Maya Patel) - Added regression tests for merge + token rollover scenarios in CI. Two flaky cases found related to clock skew between services; added synthetic tests with skewed clocks.

2026-03-12: Diego Martinez - PR for ingress idempotency keys opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/4901. Rolling to canary next week. Created follow-up ENG ticket to implement atomic merge locks (ENG-421999).
